transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-04-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (CTO, Acme), Laura Chen (Data Engineer, Acme), Marta Gomez (Head of AI, Acme)

Summary: quick sync, checking env readiness for the first throughput and latency benchmarks. Some minor access issues with S3 bucket and VPC peering; planning dedicated run.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on time. I think we have 40ish minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Ravi: Yep, Ravi here.
[00:07] Laura: Laura here.
[00:09] Marta: Marta here.
[00:12] Priya: Priya from Redwood.
[00:13] Jordan: Great. So agenda—onboarding progress, access setup, and run readiness. I'll hand off to Priya to summarize infra checks and what we need for the bench.
[00:22] Priya: Cool. Hi all. We validated the container image and the init scripts; main outstanding items are: 1) S3 test data access, 2) IAM role for Redwood runner, 3) VPC peering or private link for prod-like run, and 4) KMS key access for encrypting logs. Right now the S3 bucket policy returned a 403 when we tried the sample pull yesterday.
[00:40] Laura: Ah yeah that's on us, I opened a ticket but didn't finish the policy. I'll add a read-only role and share the ARN.
[00:45] Jordan: Awesome—if you can add a role that allows s3:GetObject for the bucket path and tag the role with redwood-automation we can pick it up. Also we need STS assume-role permissions.
[00:56] Laura: Ok, I can do that. Any preference for path structure? We have a few partitions.
[01:05] Priya: Flat path is easiest. Put the eval prompts under /redwood-eval/ and the dataset under /redwood-data/ smaller chunks. Also include a manifest file.
[01:19] Ravi: Quick question on data residency—do we need to transfer anything outside the us-east-1 region? For compliance it's important.
[01:28] Jordan: For the hosted runs we keep data in region, but for dedicated we'll spin up in your requested region. We can ensure the runner uses us-east-1. If you require no egress at all we can do VPC-only private deployment.
[01:43] Marta: And KMS—will Redwood use our CMK or your key?
[01:48] Priya: We can use your customer-managed CMK. Need kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt for the assumed role. We also need logs to be encrypted at rest—most customers prefer their key.
[02:00] Laura: I'll talk to infra—should be okay. I'll also get SAML metadata for SSO.
[02:06] Jordan: Great. Next, the bench plan—Priya?
[02:12] Priya: We're planning two runs: a latency-focused run with small batch sizes to measure p95/p99, and a throughput run on dedicated capacity targeting sustained tokens/sec. We'll use model v1.3 quantized int8 and v1.3 fp16 variants. Expect different kernel profiles.
[02:28] Marta: For our app, p95 under 300ms is ideal. Is that realistic for the quantized model?
[02:34] Priya: For short prompts 300ms p95 is tight on GPU if your prompt plus response length is long—if you keep generation length small it is possible. We can tune beam size, tokens, and kv cache re-use. For dedicated GPUs we usually hit p95 around 200-350ms for 1k token-turns depending on batch.
[02:52] Ravi: Can we schedule the dedicated run during our maintenance window? We prefer midnight to 4am.
[02:58] Jordan: Yep we can do that. We'll ask Priya to kick off the dedicated throughput run in that window.
[03:05] Priya: Sounds good. A couple of notes: 1) we need your SSH bastion IP range if you want host-level access, 2) if we do VPC peering add routes for 10.0.0.0/16 to the redwood prefix, and 3) please verify that there are no restrictive egress rules blocking our control plane.
[03:28] Laura: For the SSH bastion we usually limit to our corporate IPs; I'll share the range.
[03:35] Jordan: On security docs—Marta, you mentioned SOC2 questions last week. We can share our SOC2 report and our runbook for auditable logs.
[03:45] Marta: Yes please, and also details on access logging and retention policy.
[03:50] Jordan: We'll attach the SOC2 and our KMS guide. Expect an email from me.

[04:05] -- Transcript has more granular logs --
[04:10] [05:10] Laura: small aside, we had an error with the assume-role token: 'AccessDenied: STS assume role not authorized'
[05:18] Priya: That usually means the trust policy isn't set to allow our redwood-automation principal. When you create the role make sure the Principal includes arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-automation or we can provide exact principal.
[05:35] Laura: Ok I'll update.
[05:39] Ravi: Can you share the principal? I'll pass to infra.
[05:42] Jordan: I'll paste the principal in the follow-up slack and email.

[06:00] [08:00] Priya: On the bench scripts—we're using seq_len distributions that mirror your traffic and a set of 50 eval prompts. We'll also run a stress test for 1 hour to observe model degradation and memory growth. Please confirm the eval prompts are representative.
[08:23] Marta: We'll review and maybe swap 10 prompts—some are longer than our real-world ones.
[08:30] Priya: Perfect—if you could annotate which ones are high priority.

[09:00] [12:00] Ravi: About pricing—we briefly discussed dedicated vs hosted. Can you re-outline tradeoffs?
[12:12] Jordan: Hosted is faster to start, pay per token; dedicated is a monthly commit but predictable throughput and lower unit cost for steady volume. For this POC if you want stable latencies and isolation, dedicated for the bench makes sense.
[12:28] Marta: Ok. Also curious about fallback—if we degrade do you auto-fallback to CPU or smaller model?
[12:35] Priya: We support automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant or a different region. For critical paths we recommend multi-tier policies: local retry, then fallback model, then region fallback.

[13:00] [16:00] Laura: One more infra note—our VPC has flow logs enabled which send to customer-owned s3. Will that interfere?
[16:12] Priya: No, that's fine. We just need access to the logs for troubleshooting if you opt-in; otherwise we don't need to pull them.
[16:20] Laura: We'll opt in.

[17:00] [20:00] Jordan: Let's capture next steps—I'll go first. Jordan to send bench scripts, principal ARN, and pricing worksheet.
[20:10] Jordan: Priya will run dedicated throughput and share logs. Laura will provide IAM role and SAML metadata. Marta to confirm latency targets and eval prompts.
[20:25] Marta: I'll confirm the SLO and send annotated prompts by end of weekend.
[20:30] Laura: I'll get the role and S3 policy to you by Wednesday.

[21:00] [24:00] Priya: For the dedicated run we'll measure tokens/sec, GPU util, temperature (profiling), p95/p99 latency, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll include KV cache hit rates in the report.
[24:20] Ravi: Great. Any blockers?
[24:25] Laura: Only the IAM & KMS bits. We're on it.
[24:30] Jordan: Ok, timeline—bench run scheduled for night of 2025-04-14 pending access by 2025-04-15. If access delayed we push to week of 4/21.

[26:00] [30:00] Marta: Slight question—about model variants and quantization artifacts. Any guidance on quality regression metrics?
[30:12] Priya: We'll run Rouge/bleu-like scoring and human eval for a sample. For quantization, we'll check embedding drift and generation quality; if regression is >2% on our core prompts we flag it.
[30:35] Marta: Ok sounds good.

[31:00] [35:00] Ravi: On legal/procurement—do you need a DPA signed before we run the POC?
[35:12] Jordan: For POC we operate under a short form MSA and we can do a POC addendum. But if you require a full DPA before any data access we can expedite with our legal.
[35:30] Ravi: I'll loop in procurement and legal.

[36:00] [39:00] Laura: Quick note—we had a small transcription issue earlier where the script referenced 'KV cash' in the logs; ignore that.
[39:10] Priya: Ha, yeah transcription spells KV cache weird sometimes.
[39:20] Jordan: Alright if no other items we'll wrap and I'll send follow-ups.
[39:30] Marta: Thanks everyone.
[39:33] Ravi: Thanks.
[39:35] Jordan: Bye.

Recap / Action items repeated:
- Jordan: send bench scripts, principal ARN, pricing worksheet (due 2025-04-10)
- Laura: create IAM role, S3 read policy, share SAML metadata (due 2025-04-15)
- Priya: run dedicated throughput test in maintenance window and share logs (target 2025-04-20)
- Marta: confirm SLOs and annotate eval prompts (due 2025-04-12)

End of transcript
